rows: super() must be the first statement in a subclass constructor if it's used.
Useful when the method is overridden in the subclass and you still want to invoke the parent class version.
When both superclass and subclass have variables with the same name, super.variableName can be used to access the parent class variable.

items: Here, super.calculateEMI(principal) in HomeLoan refers to the parent Loan class method.
This demonstrates method overriding with super keyword and runtime polymorphism.
super(); calls the constructor of the parent class Loan before executing the body of the HomeLoan constructor.
super.rate accesses the parent class variable even though the child has a variable with the same name.
super() calls the immediate parent class constructor.
super.methodName() invokes the parent class method (helpful when overriding).
super.variableName accesses the parent class variable (when shadowed in child).
It promotes code reusability and helps in resolving ambiguities between superclass and subclass members.
